content.text:
The appended text has literal `\`` sequences. Let me fix them by replacing `\`` with `` ` `` in the file (only affects these, plus maybe elsewhere; let me count occurrences of `\`` in the file first). Then verify the tail looks right.

I'll use PowerShell: 
```
$c = Get-Content AUDIT_LEDGER.md -Raw
$n = ([regex]::Matches($c, '\\`')).Count
$c2 = $c -replace '\\`','`'
Set-Content -Path AUDIT_LEDGER.md -Value $c2 -NoNewline
```
Careful with PowerShell escaping of backtick (PowerShell escape character!). `-replace '\\`','`'` — in PowerShell, backtick inside single quotes is literal; regex `\\`` means backslash followed by backtick. Hmm, the pattern string in single quotes: '\\`' → characters backslash backslash backtick; regex interprets `\\` as literal backslash and `` ` `` as literal backtick ✓. Replacement '`' is literal backtick ✓ (in single quotes, regex replacement treats `$` specially but backtick is fine).

Alternatively use .NET Replace: `$c.Replace('\`','`')` — with single-quoted '\`' = backslash+backtick ✓ and replacement '`' ✓. Simpler and no regex. Let me do that, count first.

Also check that the file doesn't use "\`" elsewhere (grep).

content.name: run_code
content.arguments: {"code": "const r = await tools.pwsh({description: \"Fix escaped backticks in ledger\", command: \"$c = Get-Content AUDIT_LEDGER.md -Raw; $n = ([regex]::Matches($c, '\\\\\\\\`')).Count; Write-Output ('before=' + $n); $c2 = $c.Replace('\\\\`','`'); Set-Content -Path AUDIT_LEDGER.md -Value $c2 -NoNewline -Encoding utf8; $d = Get-Content AUDIT_LEDGER.md -Raw; Write-Output ('after=' + ([regex]::Matches($d, '\\\\\\\\`')).Count); Get-Content AUDIT_LEDGER.md -Tail 6 | Out-String -Width 240\", timeoutMs: 120000});\nconsole.log(r.kind==='foreground'? r.stdout.text + r.stderr.text : JSON.stringify(r));\n", "description": "Replace escaped backticks in ledger"}
